beaches.name: 12th Street Jetty
beaches.description: The 12th Street Jetty in Sea Isle City is called a longboarder's sanctuary — mellow roller waves perfect for cruising.

beaches.name: 1st Street Jetty
beaches.description: The 1st Street Jetty at the north end of Ocean City produces consistent rights off the rock structure.

beaches.name: 1st Street Jetty (Virginia Beach)
beaches.description: First Street is Virginia Beach's most established surf zone. The north jetty at Rudee Inlet traps sand and often produces a rideable right when nearby open beach is flat, with more push on E to SE tropical or nor'easter swell.

beaches.name: 204s
beaches.description: 204s is a beach break in San Clemente, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: 36th-42nd Street
beaches.description: The 36th-42nd Street zone in Sea Isle City produces quality lefts on NE swells, with multiple jetties offering options.

beaches.name: 38th Avenue (Santa Cruz)
beaches.description: 38th Avenue, also called Jack's by some surf reports and locals, is a user-friendly right reef that handles south and west swells. It offers long rides at lower tide and is popular with longboarders and groms.

beaches.name: 3Ms
beaches.description: 3Ms is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: 3rd Avenue Beach
beaches.description: The 3rd Avenue designated surfing zone in Bradley Beach is a known longboard spot with easy, peeling waves and a 400ft surfing area.

beaches.name: 3rd Avenue Jetty
beaches.description: The 3rd Avenue Jetty is at the north end of Belmar's beach-break stretch, where rock groins create wedgy peaks on both sides.

beaches.name: 52nd Street
beaches.description: Just north of 54th, 52nd Street serves up slightly bigger, more walled waves that require quick take-offs. The sandy bottom and jetty setup create long walls that are great for experienced surfers who like to race down the line. It works at mid tide and tends to close out on lower tides.

beaches.name: 54th Street
beaches.description: Newport's 54th Street is a high-performance beach break created by man-made jetties. It offers peaky lefts and rights over a sandy bottom and attracts some of the best local surfers. The wave works on most tides but is best at mid tide and can get very crowded.

beaches.name: 72nd Place
beaches.description: 72nd Place is the best surf spot in the Long Beach area.

beaches.name: 7th Street Beach
beaches.description: 7th Street Beach is Ocean City's most iconic surf spot, home to surfing since 1967.

beaches.name: 8th Avenue Jetty
beaches.description: 8th Avenue Jetty is one of Belmar's heaviest and most localized peaks.

beaches.name: Acapulquito (Costa Azul)
beaches.description: Acapulquito (Costa Azul) is a reef surf spot near San José del Cabo, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and inconsistent. Reported waves run right.

beaches.name: Agate Beach
beaches.description: Agate Beach is a beach break in Newport, OR. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Agate Street
beaches.description: Agate Street is a beach break in Laguna Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Ala Moana Bowls
beaches.description: Ala Moana Bowls is a legendary reef break off Magic Island known for its heaving left-hand tube and occasional right. Breaking over a shallow coral reef, Bowls offers long, hollow waves that attract expert shortboarders when a solid south or southwest swell lines up with light northerly winds. On bigger swells the barrels are thick and dangerous, and the lineup is extremely competitive.

beaches.name: Alfonsos
beaches.description: Alfonsos is a reef surf spot near Popotla, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Alisitos
beaches.description: Alisitos is a beach surf spot near La Salina, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Anahola
beaches.description: Anahola Beach on Kauaʻi's windward side is a tranquil bay protected by a fringing reef that creates a calm inner lagoon and a fun outer break when north- or east-facing swells arrive. Locals enjoy fishing, snorkeling and surfing here, and the white sand and lush backdrop make it picturesque. Watch for currents near the old pier and rocks at either end of the bay.

beaches.name: Andrew Molera State Beach (river mouth)
beaches.description: Big Sur rivermouth and point-style setup inside Andrew Molera State Park. It has right-breaking potential and meaningful access complexity.

beaches.name: Asbury Park
beaches.description: Asbury Park comprises several beach breaks around jetties, offering rights off the groins and a fun left at The Cove. It works best with southeast‑to‑east swells and offshore west winds late summer through fall.

beaches.name: Asilomar State Beach
beaches.description: Consistent Pacific Grove surf zone with exposed beach and reef options. Asilomar can handle size and includes named zones such as Roadsides, Middles, and Reef.

beaches.name: Assateague Beach (Virginia)
beaches.description: The Virginia end of Assateague is an exposed Atlantic beach break with shifting sandbars and left and right peaks. Tropical swell and nor'easters produce the most useful surf, while ordinary summer days are often small and soft.

beaches.name: Asuncion Bay
beaches.description: Asuncion Bay is a reef surf spot near Bahía Asunción, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Avalanche
beaches.description: Avalanche is a beach break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Avalon Pier
beaches.description: Avalon Pier is an iconic Outer Banks surf spot in the heart of Kill Devil Hills. The sand near the pier produces powerful, hollow peaks on both sides, drawing some of the region's best surfers. The crowd and localism can be intense, so this wave is for advanced riders who know pier etiquette.

beaches.name: Avila Beach
beaches.description: Sheltered south-facing beach in San Luis Bay with gentle waves.

beaches.name: Backwash
beaches.description: Backwash is a beach surf spot near Cabo San Lucas, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and inconsistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Backyards
beaches.description: Backyards is a broad reef zone east of Sunset with multiple powerful peaks and exposure to north and northeast swell. The open playing field can look inviting, but currents, shifting peaks, and shallow reef require advanced judgment.

beaches.name: Bahia Chileno
beaches.description: Bahia Chileno is a reef surf spot near Cabo San Lucas, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and inconsistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Bahia Tortugas (Turtle Bay)
beaches.description: Bahia Tortugas (Turtle Bay) is a beach surf spot near Bahía Tortugas, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as reasonably exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Baja Malibu
beaches.description: Baja Malibu is a beach surf spot near Tijuana, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Bandon
beaches.description: Bandon is a beach break in Bandon, OR. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Banyans
beaches.description: Banyans, along Aliʻi Drive in Kailua-Kona, is a fast, hollow reef break named after a large banyan tree that once shaded the shoreline. The wave serves up a long, powerful right and shorter left when northwest or southwest swells wrap around the island, drawing a dedicated crowd of expert surfers. Shallow reefs, sea urchins and a competitive lineup make this spot suitable only for advanced surfers.

beaches.name: Bastendorff Beach
beaches.description: This exposed beach break near Coos Bay offers reliable surf with left and right peaks. It starts at less than 3 ft and holds up to 6 ft; optimum swell is from the west with offshore southeast winds.

beaches.name: Bay Head Beach
beaches.description: Bay Head is one of the best beach breaks on the Jersey Shore — fast right-hand barrels over shallow sandbars near rock groins.

beaches.name: Bay Street
beaches.description: Bay Street is the more powerful section of Santa Monica Beach.

beaches.name: Beachbreak
beaches.description: Beachbreak is a beach surf spot near La Paz, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Beacons
beaches.description: Beacons is a reef break in Encinitas, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Belmar Beach
beaches.description: Belmar's 16th Street break is a classic beach break with shifting sandbars and peaks that break both left and right. It suits intermediate surfers and works on any tide with south‑to‑east swells and offshore west winds.

beaches.name: Belmar Fishing Pier
beaches.description: The Belmar Fishing Pier at 19th Avenue marks the south end of Belmar's mile-long beach-break stretch.

beaches.name: Big Jetty
beaches.description: Big Jetty is a jetty break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Big Rock
beaches.description: Big Rock is a heavy, hollow left-hand reef break at the foot of Palomar Avenue. It produces fast stand-up barrels on west swells and is best suited to advanced surfers due to the very shallow reef and powerful waves.

beaches.name: Birdrock
beaches.description: Birdrock is a reef break in La Jolla, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Blackies
beaches.description: Blackies is the clearest missing North OC add: a Newport Pier northside sandy beachbreak and longboard zone that works for learners on genuinely small, clean mornings.

beaches.name: Blacks Beach
beaches.description: **Blacks Beach** represents San Diego County's best beach break and California premier beach break overall, rated 9/10.

beaches.name: Bob Hall Pier
beaches.description: Bob Hall Pier at Padre Balli Park is a long-established Corpus Christi surf zone. The exposed sandbars produce lefts and rights from local windswells and stronger tropical swell, with more push than many protected Gulf beaches. Sandbar position and construction around the pier site can change the best peak.

beaches.name: Boca Del Salado
beaches.description: Boca Del Salado is a reef surf spot near Cabo Pulmo, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as fairly exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Boca De Santo Tomas
beaches.description: Boca De Santo Tomas is a reef surf spot near La Bocana, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Bodega Bay / Doran Beach
beaches.description: Doran Beach inside Bodega Bay offers gentle beach break waves ideal for beginners. The outer reefs protect the bay from larger swells, so waves are usually small, but occasional NW swells can produce fun, rippable peaks.

beaches.name: Bolinas
beaches.description: Tucked in behind Duxbury Reef, Bolinas offers soft rolling waves at the mouth of a lagoon – perfect for beginners and longboarders. The sandbars shift but there's usually a mellow left breaking off the jetty and a right across the channel.

beaches.name: Boynton Inlet
beaches.description: Boynton Inlet features a beach break and jetty with an outside sandbar that produces long hollow lefts when NE swell hits at low tide. The north side has clean, empty peaks, while the south side near the jetty offers punchy waves. It's a fun spot for intermediate surfers seeking challenging waves.

beaches.name: Brinley Avenue
beaches.description: Brinley Avenue jetty in Bradley Beach handles big E swells when everywhere else closes out — a valuable backup spot.

beaches.name: Broadway Beach
beaches.description: Broadway Beach faces south — unique in NJ — making NE winds offshore here when everywhere else is blown out.

beaches.name: Brookings (Harris Beach)
beaches.description: Brookings (Harris Beach) is a beach break in Brookings, OR. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Brooks Street
beaches.description: **Brooks Street** showcases Laguna Beach's beacon break rated 8/10 for summer/fall performance. Multiple reef tiers activate progressively: First Reef (50m out, steep/ledgy), Second Reef (95m, glassy barreling at 6-10+ feet), Third/Fourth Reefs (massive days only).

beaches.name: Cabo Colonet
beaches.description: Cabo Colonet is a point surf spot near Punta Colonet, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and rarely breaks.

beaches.name: Cabo Pulmo
beaches.description: Cabo Pulmo is a point surf spot near Cabo Pulmo, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as quite exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Cabo San Quintin
beaches.description: Cabo San Quintin is a point surf spot near Venustiano Carranza (Santa María), Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run right.

beaches.name: Calafia
beaches.description: Calafia is a point surf spot near Popotla, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: California Trailer Park
beaches.description: California Trailer Park is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Camalu
beaches.description: Camalu is a point surf spot near Camalú, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run right.

beaches.name: Campo Lopez (K-55)
beaches.description: Campo Lopez (K-55) is a reef surf spot near Primo Tapia, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Campo Renes
beaches.description: Campo Renes is a reef surf spot near Municipio de Mulegé, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: Camp Pendleton
beaches.description: The public Camp Pendleton surfing area sits beside the Virginia Army National Guard installation. Its outside sandbar can handle more E, SE, and S energy than First Street and may produce hollow sections when tide, period, and offshore wind align.

beaches.name: Campus Point (UCSB)
beaches.description: Right point with long, soft walls. Best on souths; fun on clean winter wrap.

beaches.name: Cannery (Stacks)
beaches.description: Cannery (Stacks) is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Cannon Beach (Ecola/Indian)
beaches.description: Cannon Beach (Ecola/Indian) is a beach break in Cannon Beach, OR. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Cantamar Settlement
beaches.description: Cantamar Settlement is a beach surf spot near Puerto Nuevo, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
beaches.description: At Cape Hatteras Lighthouse, jetties and sandbars focus Atlantic swells into one of the most powerful waves on the East Coast. Long, ripable lefts and dredging tubes break over shifting sandbars by the groins. The wave is fast and heavy with strong currents, making it suitable for advanced surfers only.

beaches.name: Capitola Beach
beaches.description: A protected cove in the heart of Capitola village offering gentle waves ideal for first-timers and longboarders. It needs a south swell to wrap into Monterey Bay and is often flat in winter.

beaches.name: Cardiff Reef
beaches.description: **Cardiff Reef** offers North San Diego County's best longboarding experience rated 7/10. This grass-covered flat reef produces quarter-mile rides over mellow, mushy waves ideal for multi-generational families.

beaches.name: Carlsbad State Beach
beaches.description: Carlsbad State Beach is a beach break in Carlsbad, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Carmel Beach
beaches.description: Main Carmel-by-the-Sea surf zone with several shifting beach-break peaks along the white-sand beach. Better for research as the core local spot, but conditions can change quickly with sandbars, tide, and wind.

beaches.name: Carmel River State Beach
beaches.description: A hazardous Carmel-area rivermouth and sandbar zone at Carmel River State Beach. Include for research completeness, but this is not a casual surf recommendation.

beaches.name: Carolina Beach
beaches.description: Carolina Beach is one of the most approachable beginner surf zones in North Carolina, with a gently sloping beach, forgiving summer surf, and enough room to spread out away from the busiest peaks.

beaches.name: Casas
beaches.description: Casas is a reef surf spot near El Rosario, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Cayucos Pier (south side)
beaches.description: User-friendly Central Coast beachbreak with consistent bars by the pier.

beaches.name: Cerritos Point
beaches.description: Cerritos Point is a point surf spot near El Pescadero, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Chun’s Reef
beaches.description: Chun’s Reef offers approachable right and left reef waves on smaller North Shore days, with longer walls that suit mid-lengths and longboards. It becomes faster, heavier, and less forgiving as winter swell grows.

beaches.name: Church
beaches.description: Church sits in the San Onofre / Trestles-area south of San Mateo Creek, but public surf traffic usually approaches it from the San Clemente/Trestles side. It is a cobblestone beach and rivermouth setup with point-like right walls when west swell and enough tide line up. South pulses spread the lineup into multiple peaks, and bigger southwest swells can make the wave feel much more serious than its mellow reputation.

beaches.name: Cielito Lindo
beaches.description: Cielito Lindo is a beach surf spot near Ejido Nueva Odisea (El Pabellón), Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Clam Beach
beaches.description: Clam Beach is a broad, exposed public sand beach north of the Little River. County access and facilities are verified, but reliable spot-level surf, tide, and skill guidance is too limited to promote it as a recommendation.

beaches.name: Coast Guard Beach
beaches.description: Part of the Cape Cod National Seashore, Coast Guard Beach offers mellow waves over shifting sandbars and is popular with beginners and families. The break works best on northeast‑to‑southeast swells with southwest to west‑northwest winds and low to mid tides.

beaches.name: Cocoa Beach Pier
beaches.description: The Cocoa Beach Pier is Florida's most famous surf landmark and home to legends like Kelly Slater. The pier breaks on almost every type of swell, with chest‑ to head‑high north swells producing the best waves. It's a mellow wave well suited to beginners and longboarders but can offer punchier sections when hurricane swells wrap in.

beaches.name: College Cove
beaches.description: College Cove is a sheltered cove within Trinidad State Beach, but its access trail is closed because of erosion. The spot is retained for map and closure awareness and must not be recommended or indexed while the closure remains in effect.

beaches.name: Corolla
beaches.description: Corolla is the most beginner-friendly Outer Banks call when you want the broad, sandy feel of the northern beaches without the punchier setups farther south.

beaches.name: Corona del Mar
beaches.description: Beachbreak near 15th Street and the river mouth with peaks that work best on SSW/WNW combo swells. Mid tide provides the best shape. When the river is flowing, peaks can get rippy. The river mouth creates a strong rip that can be turbo on big tide swings. Parking via meters and neighborhood streets.

beaches.name: Coronado North Jetty
beaches.description: Coronado North Jetty is a jetty break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Cottons
beaches.description: Cottons is the northern end of the Trestles cluster at San Mateo Point and is best understood as a Trestles / San Onofre border-zone wave with San Clemente surf taxonomy. The wave is a cobblestone point-and-reef style left that often breaks farther offshore than nearby peaks and can feel softer on average swells. Larger, longer-period south swells and lower tide add speed, shape, and more consequence through the inside.

beaches.name: County Line
beaches.description: County Line, on the border of LA and Ventura counties, features a right-hand cobblestone reef break at the northern end and 500 yards of beach break to the south. Conditions range from peaky lefts and rights to heavy closeouts. On larger swells, currents and rips become strong and the point turns into an advanced wave.

beaches.name: Crash Boat
beaches.description: Crash Boat is a popular Aguadilla family beach with a picturesque pier and a user-friendly beach break. On small north to northwest swells, the sandy peaks are one of the better beginner and longboard options on Puerto Rico's west side. The beach gets busy with swimmers, snorkelers, and boats, so the safe beginner read is small surf, clear flags, and plenty of room away from the pier traffic.

beaches.name: Croatan Beach
beaches.description: South Croatan is an open beach break beside Camp Pendleton. It favors SE tropical swell and offers more room than the jetty peak, with shifting outside bars that can produce left and right walls.

beaches.name: Croatan Jetty
beaches.description: Croatan Jetty is the north end of Croatan Beach, where a wooden groin and Rudee Inlet's south jetty can bend swell into a predominantly left wedge. It is fickle but becomes punchier around high tide during nor'easters.

beaches.name: Crystal Beach
beaches.description: Crystal Beach is an open beach break on the Bolivar Peninsula with shifting sandbars and left and right peaks. It is usually small and wind-driven, but stronger east and southeast swells can produce workable surf along the broad shoreline.

beaches.name: Crystal Cove
beaches.description: **Crystal Cove** offers scenic but fickle left point/reef rated 5/10, working on south to southwest swells (170-230°, center 200°) with northeast winds (45°).

beaches.name: Crystal Pier
beaches.description: Crystal Pier is a jetty break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: C Street / Ventura Point
beaches.description: A long right-hand point break that peels down several sections with room for shortboards and longboards. Multiple take-off peaks mean it can handle a crowd, but it's often busy with locals and traveling surfers. Good for intermediate riders who can navigate cobblestones and shifting peaks.

beaches.name: Deerfield Beach Pier
beaches.description: Deerfield Beach Pier offers a small, often mushy wave that's popular with locals and tourists. Surfing is only allowed north of the pier, where high‑performance waves break in the hot zone; south of lifeguard tower 7 has softer waves for learners. Hazards include rip currents, pollution, theft and the occasional shark.

beaches.name: Del Mar
beaches.description: **Del Mar** (15th Street) represents rare reef amid miles of beachbreak, rated 7/10. Left-hand reef break (dominant) with shorter right receives swells 200-320° (center 250°).

beaches.name: Del Mar Rivermouth
beaches.description: Beachbreak near 15th Street and the river mouth with peaks that work best on SSW/WNW combo swells. Mid tide provides the best shape. When the river is flowing, peaks can get rippy. The river mouth creates a strong rip that can be turbo on big tide swings. Parking via meters and neighborhood streets.

beaches.name: Del Monte Beach
beaches.description: Monterey beach-break and sandbar zone. Del Monte is an exposed beach break and sandbar with winter as the favored season.

beaches.name: Devereux / Sands (Coal Oil Point)
beaches.description: Open pocket west of Campus with peaky beach/reef setups.

beaches.name: Diamond Head (Cliffs)
beaches.description: Diamond Head Cliffs is a long stretch of reef along the slopes of Leʻahi where multiple peaks offer rippable lefts and occasional rights. The waves are consistent year-round and handle a variety of swell directions, but they break over sharp lava and coral that require confident paddling and knowledge of the currents. Getting there involves a hike down the bluff and a long paddle, and the lineup can be crowded when the south swell pulses.

beaches.name: Ditch Plains
beaches.description: Ditch Plains is Montauk's famed reef break: a rocky bottom produces long peeling A‑frame waves that break both left and right. It's suitable for longboards and funboards and works best on south‑to‑southeast swells with mid to high tides; summer and fall see friendly crowds but locals still hold priority.

beaches.name: Dockweiler State Beach
beaches.description: Dockweiler State Beach is a hidden gem for LA surfers looking to escape crowds.

beaches.name: Doheny Beach
beaches.description: **Doheny State Beach** offers Orange County's second-easiest learning wave after San O' Dogpatch, rated 4/10 overall but 6/10 for beginners.

beaches.name: Doheny State Beach
beaches.description: **Doheny State Beach** offers Orange County's second-easiest learning wave after San O' Dogpatch, rated 4/10 overall but 6/10 for beginners.

beaches.name: Domes
beaches.description: Domes is a classic Rincón reef break known for its powerful hollow right-hand waves. It handles N–NW swells and works best with SE offshore winds. Intermediate and advanced surfers enjoy long, fast walls and the occasional barrel, but the shallow reef and busy lineup mean caution is essential.

beaches.name: D Street
beaches.description: D Street is a beach break in Encinitas, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Dunes
beaches.description: Dunes is a beach surf spot near La Misión, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: El Capitan
beaches.description: When a strong west swell wraps into this secluded point, El Capitan can produce 300-yard right-handers with barrel sections, but it's fickle and often flat. The take-off is steep over boulders and reef, making it best for experienced surfers.

beaches.name: El Cardon
beaches.description: El Cardon is a point surf spot near Municipio de San Quintín, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: El Cocal
beaches.description: El Cocal, also mapped as Playa El Guano, is a southeast Puerto Rico beachbreak in Camino Nuevo, Yabucoa. It has scenic rock formations and a nearby natural pool, while the surf zone can produce inconsistent left and right peaks when south to southeast swell reaches the coast. Treat it as a lower-intermediate call because shorebreak, rocks, rips, and missing lifeguard coverage matter even when the wave looks playful.

beaches.name: El Morro Point (K37.5)
beaches.description: El Morro Point (K37.5) is a point surf spot near Popotla, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: El Paso
beaches.description: El Paso is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: El Pescadero
beaches.description: El Pescadero is a reef surf spot near El Pescadero, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: El Porto (Manhattan)
beaches.description: **El Porto** (Manhattan Beach) functions as South Bay's northwest swell magnet rated 7/10 for consistency despite variable quality.

beaches.name: El Rincon
beaches.description: El Rincon is a beach surf spot near Municipio de Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as sheltered and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: El Segundo Beach Jetty
beaches.description: The El Segundo Jetty is a reliable breakwater break just south of LAX. It picks up southwest swells and offers lefts and rights. Summer brings the most consistent surf, and the best conditions occur when a southwest swell meets a northeast offshore wind. The surf is rarely crowded but pollution and man-made obstacles can be issues.

beaches.name: El Socorro
beaches.description: El Socorro is a point surf spot near Municipio de San Quintín, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: Emma Wood
beaches.description: A mix of reef and sand peaks with a punchy take-off that mellows into long walls when the reef section lights up. The spot catches most swells and can produce long right and left walls around the offshore reef.

beaches.name: Ensenada Beaches
beaches.description: Ensenada Beaches is a beach surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Flagler Beach
beaches.description: Flagler Beach is a long coquina‑sand beach known for its thumping shorebreak and friendly surf culture. On low incoming tide the second sandbar produces fun rights and lefts when west winds and swell align. The area near the pier can get crowded and powerful; novices should surf a few blocks away.

beaches.name: Florence South Jetty
beaches.description: **Florence South Jetty** offers challenging river mouth break rated 6/10 but fickle and dangerous. Siuslaw River south jetty produces inside left (harbor entrance wave—wedgy, hollow) and outside beach rights.

beaches.name: Folly Beach
beaches.description: Folly Beach is a long barrier island south of Charleston with several fun breaks. The Washout—a stretch blown open by Hurricane Hugo—produces punchy peaks on SE‑NE swells, while the Folly Beach Pier offers long lefts on the south side. It's friendly for beginners when small but can handle good size during hurricane season.

beaches.name: Forster St. Oceanside
beaches.description: Forster St. Oceanside is a beach break in Oceanside, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Fort Point (San Francisco)
beaches.description: A novelty right-hand reef that breaks directly under the Golden Gate Bridge. When a big west swell refracts around Land's End, Fort Point offers long peeling rights with a spectacular backdrop. It's fickle and often crowded with locals.

beaches.name: Frailes South
beaches.description: Frailes South is a reef surf spot near Cabo Frailes, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as fairly exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Galveston – 61st Street Pier
beaches.description: The beach at 61st Street is one of Galveston's established Seawall surf zones. The pier and nearby structures influence the sandbars, producing short lefts and rights when Gulf windswells reach the island. Smaller days suit longboards and learners, while storm-driven surf brings stronger currents and a more demanding paddle.

beaches.name: Galveston – Pleasure Pier
beaches.description: Pleasure Pier is a named Galveston surf break along the central Seawall. Shifting sandbars around the pier can organize Gulf windswells into rideable peaks on either side. The waves are usually short-period and modest, but cold fronts and tropical systems can produce faster, stronger surf.

beaches.name: Garrapata State Beach (southern coves)
beaches.description: Remote, exposed beach-break zone on the north Big Sur coast. Garrapata is a coastal state park surf zone with meaningful rips, undertow, rocks, and shark risk.

beaches.name: George's
beaches.description: George's is a beach break in Cardiff-by-the-Sea, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Ghost Tree
beaches.description: Rare, expert-only big-wave reef off Pescadero Point. This should be treated as a research-only listing unless Quiver has a dedicated expert and big-wave context.

beaches.name: Gold Beach (South Jetty)
beaches.description: **Gold Beach** (South Jetty) produces fickle hollow rights rated 5/10 at Rogue River mouth. Stubby jetty facing southwest creates right wedges.

beaches.name: Goldenwest
beaches.description: North HB Streets is a beach break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Grandview Beach
beaches.description: **Grandview** provides beginner-friendly Leucadia beachbreak rated 6/10. Rock bottom covered by sand creates inside beachbreak and outside reef breaks.

beaches.name: Haleʻiwa Aliʻi Beach
beaches.description: Haleʻiwa Aliʻi Beach is the North Shore gateway reef at the west end of Haleʻiwa. Its powerful right wraps toward the harbor on winter north and northwest swell, with current, shallow inside reef, and a competitive takeoff requiring advanced judgment when size rises.

beaches.name: Halfway House
beaches.description: Halfway House is a beach surf spot near La Misión, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Hampton Beach
beaches.description: Hampton Beach is a fun sand‑bottom beach break with peaks up to 100 m and a reef around the headland producing fast lefts. Best conditions occur with offshore northwest winds and swells from the east, northeast or southeast, working at mid to high tide.

beaches.name: Hanalei Bay (Kauai)
beaches.description: **Hanalei Bay** (Kauai) offers scenic North Shore point break rated 7/10. Main break is long right point on eastern side of crescent bay breaking up to 300 yards over lava reef.

beaches.name: Hanalei (Wainiha) — Colony Resort
beaches.description: Hanalei (Wainiha) — Colony Resort is a reef/point break in Hanalei, HI. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for strong currents, shallow reef on low tide.

beaches.name: Hapuna Beach (Kohala)
beaches.description: Hapuna Beach (Kohala) is a beach break in Waimea, HI. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents.

beaches.name: HB Cliffs
beaches.description: HB Cliffs is a beach break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Hermosa Beach Pier
beaches.description: Hermosa Beach Pier produces consistent peaks on both sides of the pier.

beaches.name: Hermosa Beach South
beaches.description: South Hermosa offers a mellower beach break experience.

beaches.name: Hermosa Pier
beaches.description: Hermosa Pier is a jetty break in Hermosa Beach, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Higgins Beach
beaches.description: Higgins Beach is a southeast‑facing stretch that picks up tropical storm and nor'easter swells. It features both beach‑break peaks and a rocky point; the bottom is sand and rock, and local surfers are protective but welcoming to respectful visitors.

beaches.name: Hobuck Beach (Neah Bay)
beaches.description: Hobuck Beach is a remote, crescent-shaped beach on the Makah Reservation. It offers fun peaks for beginners to intermediates and stunning views of Cape Flattery. Camping and cabins are available, and surfers often spot sea lions and jellyfish. A Makah Recreation Permit is required for access and camping.

beaches.name: Honolua Bay
beaches.description: Honolua Bay on West Maui is regarded as one of the best right-hand point breaks on Earth. The wave peels along a rocky headland in several sections, offering long barreling walls when north or northwest swells wrap into the bay. Crowds of experts flock here during the winter season, and the coral reef demands precision and respect.

beaches.name: Ho'okipa
beaches.description: Hoʻokipa Beach Park on Maui's north shore is world famous for windsurfing and kitesurfing but also has excellent surf for experts. Multiple breaks—from the right-hand Pavilions to the fast left at Lanes—offer powerful waves over a shallow reef, and the trades can quickly turn the lineup into a challenging windswept arena. Beginners should stay on the sand and watch, as currents and urchins pose real dangers.

beaches.name: Horseshoe
beaches.description: Horseshoe is a reef break in La Jolla, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Hotel Del Coronado
beaches.description: Hotel Del Coronado is a beach break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Houda Point / Camel Rock
beaches.description: Houda Point and Camel Rock form a rocky, partially sheltered surf zone north of Moonstone. The land-trust access page identifies lower-tide swell as the established surf opportunity; the representative pin sits in the nearshore surf zone rather than at the bluff parking area.

beaches.name: Humbug Mountain (Port Orford)
beaches.description: Humbug Mountain (Port Orford) is a beach break in Port Orford, OR. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Huntington Beach Pier
beaches.description: Huntington Beach Pier is a jetty break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Huntington Beach Pier Northside
beaches.description: Huntington Beach Pier Northside is a jetty break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Huntington Beach Pier Southside
beaches.description: Huntington Beach Pier Southside is a jetty break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Huntington St.
beaches.description: Huntington St. is a beach break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Huntington State Beach
beaches.description: Huntington State Beach is a beach break in Huntington Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Imperial Beach
beaches.description: Imperial Beach is a beach break in Imperial Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Imperial Beach Pier
beaches.description: Imperial Beach Pier is a jetty break in Imperial Beach, CA. It is suited for intermediate-advanced surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, strong currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Inches
beaches.description: Inches is the Patillas surf spot just off PR-3 on Puerto Rico's southeast coast. Local surf guides and Surfline describe it as one of the better summer and hurricane-swell spots in the area, with a left-point feel and rides that can run when the ESE swell is right. The bottom is reef, rock, coral, and river-stone style cobble rather than soft sand, so this belongs in the intermediate bucket.

beaches.name: Indicators
beaches.description: Around the corner from Domes, Indicators is named for the exposed rock that marks the takeoff. This long right‑hand point provides a good gauge of swell size for the Rincón area. It's mostly surfed by experienced locals because the takeoff is close to a shallow, exposed reef, and the wave bowls as it wraps into the bay.

beaches.name: Islas de Todos Santos
beaches.description: Islas de Todos Santos is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Isle of Palms
beaches.description: Isle of Palms (IOP) is a mellow beach break just north of Charleston. It picks up less north swell than Folly due to its slightly southerly orientation but still provides consistent waves for beginners and lower‑intermediate surfers. During late summer and early fall, tropical storm swells provide punchier surf and more push.

beaches.name: Jacksonville Beach Pier
beaches.description: Jacksonville Beach Pier juts into the Atlantic and collects swell on both sides. The sandbars around the pier produce forgiving peaks that are perfect for learning and longboarding, though they can pack a punch during hurricane season. It's a community gathering spot with a friendly vibe.

beaches.name: Jalama Beach
beaches.description: Remote and exposed beach break known for powerful, hollow peaks and long walls when sandbars align. Jalama picks up any swell and can be world-class on a clean NW swell, but currents are strong and the water is cold.

beaches.name: Jobos
beaches.description: Jobos is Isabela's iconic surf beach, with a powerful outside reef and a softer inside/sand section. The outside peak remains an intermediate-plus wave, but the inside zone supports surf schools, longboards, foam boards, and careful beginners on smaller days. Treat the spot as beginner-usable only when the swell is small and the lesson/inside area is clearly separated from the main reef takeoff.

beaches.name: K-181
beaches.description: K-181 is a reef surf spot near Punta Colonet, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: K-38
beaches.description: K-38 is a reef surf spot near Popotla, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: K-40
beaches.description: K-40 is a reef surf spot near Puerto Nuevo, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: K-55 1/2
beaches.description: K-55 1/2 is a point surf spot near La Salina, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left.

beaches.name: Kahalu'u
beaches.description: Kahaluʻu Beach Park south of Kailua-Kona is a small bay protected by a man-made breakwater that creates calm water for snorkeling and swimming. The northern corner of the bay features a gentle reef break that produces soft rollers perfect for beginners learning to surf or SUP. Watch for slippery lava rocks and keep an eye on turtles and other marine life that frequent the bay.

beaches.name: Kaisers
beaches.description: Kaisers is a fast, high-performance right near the Ala Wai harbor entrance. Clean south swell can produce steep walls and barrels over shallow reef, with boat traffic adding a serious navigation hazard.

beaches.name: Kalapaki Beach
beaches.description: Kalapaki Beach in Līhue is a crescent of golden sand sheltered by a breakwall that tames the waves and creates calm waters perfect for swimming and learning to surf. Surfers enjoy small, fun peaks near the river mouth and harbor entrance on modest east or northeast swells. The beach fronts a resort with amenities, making it a family-friendly spot but still requiring awareness of currents near the harbor.

beaches.name: Kekaha / Pakala (Infinities)
beaches.description: Pakala, also known as Infinities, is a long left-hand point break on Kauaʻi's west side near Kekaha. On summer south swells the wave peels for hundreds of meters over a shallow coral reef, making it a dream for goofy-footers who can handle the long paddle and occasional strong currents. The vibe is mellow but respect the local surfers and watch for sea urchins in the channel.

beaches.name: Kewalo Basin
beaches.description: Kewalo Basin is a high-performance south-shore reef break with fast lefts and rights near the harbor entrance. A clean south swell can produce punchy walls, but the shallow reef and active boat channel demand awareness.

beaches.name: Kill Devil Hills
beaches.description: Kill Devil Hills features multiple sandbar peaks along a gently sloping beach. The waves are generally softer than Hatteras, making it a great training ground for lower‑intermediate surfers. Swells from NE to SE light up the peaks, and winter nor'easters can produce overhead surf.

beaches.name: Kook Bay (Spring Lake)
beaches.description: Commonly called Kook Bay or Surfer's Beach, this is Spring Lake's most popular surfing beach.

beaches.name: Kure Beach
beaches.description: Kure Beach gives beginners a quieter, less hectic version of the same soft summer surf that makes southern North Carolina so usable for first sessions.

beaches.name: La Bocana (Abreojos / Mulegé Municipality)
beaches.description: La Bocana (Abreojos / Mulegé Municipality) is a point surf spot near Estero de la Bocana, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: La Bocana (Todos Santos Area)
beaches.description: La Bocana (Todos Santos Area) is a beach surf spot near Todos Santos, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: La Fonda
beaches.description: La Fonda is a point surf spot near La Misión, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left.

beaches.name: Lahaina Harbor (Breakwall)
beaches.description: Lahaina Harbor's Breakwall is a popular surf break in the heart of Lahaina, with an inside section used by surf schools and an outside section that produces steep lefts on a good south swell. The wave breaks beside the harbor's jetty over a shallow reef, so it gets shallow at low tide, but a mid-to-high tide provides fun walls up to head high. Crowds are heavy and the name "Snakewall" reflects the constant jockeying for position.

beaches.name: La Jolla Shores
beaches.description: **La Jolla Shores** functions as San Diego's most popular beginner beach, rated 7/10 for learning environment.

beaches.name: La Laguna
beaches.description: La Laguna is a beach surf spot near Mulegé, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: La Mision
beaches.description: La Mision is a reef surf spot near La Misión, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Laniakea
beaches.description: Laniakea is a long North Shore right over reef with a shorter left and enough room to show several sections. It works on winter north and northwest swell and becomes powerful as period and size increase.

beaches.name: La Ocho
beaches.description: La Ocho sits by Escambron just east of Old San Juan and gives the capital a real longboard reef option. The wave breaks over reef and rock, spreads across a large area, and can suit many ability levels when small. It is not as soft as Pine Grove, but its protected setup, board-rental access, and rolling rights make it a useful longboard and progressing-beginner page when size is manageable.

beaches.name: La Pared
beaches.description: La Pared is Luquillo's accessible town beachbreak and the best current Quiver fit for northeast Puerto Rico learner intent. Surf schools and rentals operate nearby, and small northeast to east swells create approachable peaks for beginners and longboards. The same beach can also develop strong rip currents and punchier surf, so beginner suitability depends on size, flags, and local instruction.

beaches.name: La Pastora
beaches.description: La Pastora is a point surf spot near Todos Santos, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: La Pozita
beaches.description: La Pozita is the local-name north-side El Cocal sub-break in Camino Nuevo, Yabucoa. Public beach sources generally describe La Posita or La Pocita as the semi-protected rocky pocket at Playa El Cocal rather than a standalone surf guide spot. Quiver lists it separately because local feedback says the sets can be more organized and less shorebreak-heavy than main El Cocal, while keeping it in the intermediate, local-knowledge-dependent bucket.

beaches.name: La Punta
beaches.description: La Punta is a reef surf spot near Cabo San Lucas, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run right.

beaches.name: La Push — First Beach
beaches.description: **La Push** (First Beach) delivers Olympic Peninsula's reliable spot rated 6/10 but fickle. Crescent of black sand at Quillayute River mouth features reef/cobblestone break.

beaches.name: La Push – Second Beach
beaches.description: This wide sandy beach on the Olympic Coast offers playful waist- to head-high waves ideal for longboarding and cruising. Logs and driftwood line the shore, and cold, clear water keeps crowds thin. Access requires a forest trail hike with scenic sea stacks and sea caves.

beaches.name: La Push – Third Beach
beaches.description: A bit more exposed than Second Beach, Third Beach offers longer rides and more powerful peaks. Access involves a 1.3-mile hike with a steep descent and driftwood crossing. Logs and rips demand caution, but the remote setting keeps crowds low.

beaches.name: La Salina
beaches.description: La Salina is a beach surf spot near La Salina, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Las Barrancas
beaches.description: Las Barrancas is a reef surf spot near Las Barrancas, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and inconsistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: La Selva
beaches.description: La Selva is a secluded surf zone within the Northeast Ecological Corridor near Luquillo. A NE swell wraps into the headland, producing a right‑hand point wave with adjacent beach‑break peaks. Intermediate and advanced surfers enjoy 4–8 ft waves in an unspoiled setting backed by palms and El Yunque rainforest. Access requires a hike or 4×4 and the area is protected as a sea‑turtle reserve.

beaches.name: Las Gaviotas
beaches.description: Las Gaviotas is a reef surf spot near Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Latigo Point
beaches.description: Latigo Point is a right-hand point break that offers a less crowded alternative.

beaches.name: Leadbetter
beaches.description: Soft point/inside reef near the harbor with longboard-friendly lines.

beaches.name: Leo Carrillo State Beach
beaches.description: Leo Carrillo is a family-friendly state beach with a gentle beach break.

beaches.name: Lighthouse (Punta San Jose)
beaches.description: Lighthouse (Punta San Jose) is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Little Island Fishing Pier
beaches.description: Little Island is the southern public anchor of Sandbridge. The fishing pier influences nearby sandbars, and the city maintains a surfing beach north of the structure with room for small-wave progression and stronger storm-swell peaks.

beaches.name: Long Beach
beaches.description: Long Beach is a stretch of sandy shoreline punctuated by jetties that focus swells into hollow peaks. It's a classic beach break that can serve up tubing sections on south‑ and southeast‑swell days with offshore north winds.

beaches.name: Long Beach (Boardwalk)
beaches.description: Long Beach (Boardwalk) is a beach break in Long Beach, WA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Long Branch Beach
beaches.description: Long Branch features a wide sand beach backed by a bustling promenade and restaurants. Its sandbars produce mellow peaks for lower‑intermediate surfers, but strong rip currents and occasional jellyfish and stingrays mean caution is needed.

beaches.name: Los Frailes
beaches.description: Los Frailes is a reef surf spot near Cabo Frailes, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent.

beaches.name: Lovers Point
beaches.description: A left point and cove setup at Pacific Grove. Winter is the most consistent window, with the wave wrapping into a rocky cove.

beaches.name: Lower Trestles
beaches.description: **Lower Trestles** stands as California's proving ground for progressive surfing, rated 9/10 for wave quality.

beaches.name: Makaha
beaches.description: Mākaha is a historic west-side reef and point break with powerful, long rights and occasional lefts. Winter north and northwest swell can turn it into a serious big-wave venue; smaller days still demand reef awareness and respect for the established lineup.

beaches.name: Makapuʻu
beaches.description: Makapuʻu is an exposed windward beach known for energetic shorebreak, bodysurfing, and short surfable peaks. Trade swell is frequent, but current, rocks, and heavy shorebreak make it unsuitable for novice board surfers when active.

beaches.name: Malibu First Point (Surfrider)
beaches.description: Malibu First Point (Surfrider) is a point break in Malibu, CA. It is well suited for beginners and those learning to surf. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins.

beaches.name: Malibu Second Point
beaches.description: Second Point is the middle section of the famous Malibu point break system.

beaches.name: Malibu Surfrider (First Point)
beaches.description: Malibu First Point is one of the most iconic surf breaks in the world. This cobblestone point produces long, peeling right-handers perfect for longboarding.

beaches.name: Malibu Third Point
beaches.description: Third Point is the outermost and most powerful section of Malibu.

beaches.name: Mambo Beach
beaches.description: Mambo Beach is a hollow beach-break at the north end of Spring Lake, punchier than the mellow Washington zone.

beaches.name: Manasquan Inlet
beaches.description: Manasquan Inlet is renowned as one of the East Coast's premier jetty breaks. The inlet amplifies south swells into long, powerful right‑hand walls, and competitions are held here when conditions line up.

beaches.name: Manhattan Beach Pier
beaches.description: The sandbars north and south of Manhattan Beach Pier provide consistent beach-break peaks with both lefts and rights. Summer southwest swells and offshore east winds create the best conditions. The waves can be fun for intermediates but rips are common and the lineup is often crowded.

beaches.name: María's
beaches.description: María's is a celebrated right‑hand point break that offers long, manageable rides over a shallow reef. The wave can handle large winter swells, making it a contest venue during the surf season. Intermediate surfers will enjoy its predictability, but during big swells it becomes challenging and attracts pros and strong locals.

beaches.name: Marina State Beach
beaches.description: Exposed Monterey Bay beach break north of Monterey. It can produce challenging beach-break barrels when conditions line up.

beaches.name: Marine Street Beach
beaches.description: Marine Street Beach is a beach break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Marisol
beaches.description: Marisol is a point surf spot near Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Marisol North Point
beaches.description: Marisol North Point is a point surf spot near Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Matagorda
beaches.description: Matagorda is Texas's premier surf destination where the Colorado River meets the Gulf of Mexico. Deep offshore waters meet shallow sandbars to produce powerful waves and a long left point break near the river mouth. Fast, explosive beach breaks at the jetties can pound over shallow areas and are best suited to advanced surfers.

beaches.name: Matunuck
beaches.description: Matunuck (Deep Hole) is a sheltered reef/point break that serves up long peeling waves ideal for longboards. It works best on southeast swells with north‑northwest winds; hazards include rocks, rip currents and undertow.

beaches.name: Mavericks
beaches.description: One of the most famous big-wave spots on Earth, Mavericks breaks a half-mile offshore over a shallow reef, producing giant right and left walls when long-period NW swells march in. Only expert big-wave surfers with safety teams should attempt it.

beaches.name: Mesa Lane
beaches.description: A rarely surfed reef break accessed via 240 steep steps, Mesa Lane offers both lefts and rights over a rocky bottom and works best on a rising tide with a west swell. Local surfers favour this spot after work and school.

beaches.name: Middles
beaches.description: Middles is a beach break in San Onofre, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Middles Isabela
beaches.description: Middles Isabela is a broad, multi-peak beach between Jobos and Shacks. The western end can get powerful and hollow, but the more open sand-bottom sections and surf-school use make the spot useful for progressing beginners and longboarders when the swell is small. It is a better recommendation for learners who already understand rip currents than for a first solo paddle-out.

beaches.name: Migrino
beaches.description: Migrino is a point surf spot near Municipio de Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Millers Landing
beaches.description: Millers Landing is a point surf spot near Santa Rosalillita, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left.

beaches.name: Mirador Viewpoint
beaches.description: Mirador Viewpoint is a reef surf spot near Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent.

beaches.name: Mission Beach
beaches.description: **Mission Beach** serves as central San Diego surfing bellwether rated 6/10. Nearly 2-mile stretch from South Mission Jetty to Pacific Beach offers year-round beachbreak.

beaches.name: Mission Beach (Central)
beaches.description: Beachbreak at South Mission with a jetty that creates wedging waves. Big parking lot fills with volleyball crowds mid-day. Mid tide steadies the wave shape. Onshores wreck afternoons so go early for best conditions. The jetty rip runs hard on overhead pulses - keep eyes on the current.

beaches.name: Mitchell's Cove
beaches.description: A reefy cove along West Cliff Drive that offers wedgy peaks and occasional barrels on W and NW swells. It's also a popular dog beach, so expect pups running around the sand.

beaches.name: Monastery Beach / San Jose Creek Beach
beaches.description: Monastery Beach is included only as an expert and hazard research entry. Reliable public sources emphasize scuba use and dangerous water conditions more than ordinary surf use.

beaches.name: Mondos Beach
beaches.description: A mellow, rolling wave that breaks over a gently sloping sandbar and cobblestones, ideal for longboards and learners. Mondos picks up most swell directions and has a friendly, welcoming vibe.

beaches.name: Monuments
beaches.description: Monuments is a point surf spot near El Tezal, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and very consistent. Reported waves run left.

beaches.name: Moonlight State Beach
beaches.description: Moonlight State Beach is a beach break in Encinitas, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Moonstone Beach / Little River
beaches.description: Moonstone is a public, west-facing sand beach at the Little River mouth. It is one of Humboldt County's most established surf beaches, with shifting left and right peaks that range from approachable on small days to powerful in winter swell.

beaches.name: Morro Rock / Sandspit (inside bend)
beaches.description: Inside Sandspit bend with wrapping peaks and easier channels than the outer bars.

beaches.name: Moss Landing
beaches.description: Consistent exposed beach break near the Moss Landing harbor and river area. It often works, with winter favored and ESE wind plus NW swell as the model.

beaches.name: Mustang Island State Park
beaches.description: Mustang Island State Park provides more than five miles of open Gulf beach where shifting sandbars create uncrowded left and right peaks. The surf is generally softer than Packery or Bob Hall, making smaller clean days useful for longboards and progressing surfers.

beaches.name: Nags Head Beach
beaches.description: Nags Head offers a stretch of east‑facing Outer Banks beach with numerous peaks. Sandbars create fun lefts and rights that break best on moderate swells. It's a go‑to spot for intermediate surfers looking for variety and less intimidating surf than Hatteras.

beaches.name: Nantasket Beach
beaches.description: Nantasket Beach in Hull is a long, flat beach break facing northeast on the southern end and southeast on the northern end. It handles winter storm swells and offers forgiving waves for beginners; best conditions include northeast swells and southwest winds at high tide.

beaches.name: Narragansett Town Beach
beaches.description: Narragansett Town Beach faces southeast and offers consistent beach‑break waves that tend to close out. It performs best on 4–6 ft swells with 10‑second periods and northwest winds; hazards include a sunken barge and old pier near the North Pavilion that become exposed at low tide.

beaches.name: Nauset Beach
beaches.description: Nauset Beach is an exposed beach break on outer Cape Cod known for its consistency and power. It works best on southeast swells with offshore west winds and offers both left and right peaks; strong rip currents and occasional great white shark sightings add to the drama.

beaches.name: Navarre Beach Pier
beaches.description: Navarre Beach is a long, mostly mushy beach break that's ideal for beginners of all ages. Sandbars between the pier and the park provide plenty of room to spread out. Waves are best at low tide on SE–SW swells, with light NW winds cleaning up the face.

beaches.name: Nelscott Reef
beaches.description: Half a mile off Lincoln City, Nelscott Reef is Oregon's big-wave arena where west swells and east winds produce 25-50 ft monsters. Only expert surfers with jetski support attempt this outer reef.

beaches.name: New Break (Nubes)
beaches.description: New Break (Nubes) is a beach break in San Diego, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Newport 56th St
beaches.description: Newport 56th St is a beach break in Newport Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Newport Lower Jetties
beaches.description: Newport Lower Jetties is a beach break in Newport Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Newport Point
beaches.description: **Newport Point** breaks only on hurricane swells with specific southeast component (160-190°, center 175°), rated 9/10 when working but extremely rare.

beaches.name: Newport Upper Jetties
beaches.description: Newport Upper Jetties is a beach break in Newport Beach, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: New Smyrna Beach (NSB) Inlet
beaches.description: The south side of Ponce Inlet at New Smyrna Beach is renowned for consistent, peeling waves and is a mecca for Florida surfers. Rock ledges offshore create excellent wave shape while protecting swimmers from undertow. Both accomplished surfers and beginners enjoy long rides, though shark encounters are more common here than anywhere else in the U.S.

beaches.name: Nine Palms
beaches.description: Nine Palms is a point surf spot near El Cardón, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as fairly exposed and consistent. Reported waves run right.

beaches.name: North End
beaches.description: North End covers the residential oceanfront north of the resort district. Its open sandbars are less structure-dependent than the city's jetty breaks and can provide clean longboard peaks on small swell or faster walls when tropical and winter energy arrives.

beaches.name: Ocean Beach
beaches.description: **Ocean Beach** delivers San Diego's most consistent surf rated 8/10 but most dangerous beach. Receives all swell directions 200-310° (center 270°) with east offshore winds (90°).

beaches.name: Ocean Beach Pier
beaches.description: Powerful beachbreak near the OB Pier with shifting sandbars that can handle serious size. The pier creates banks that often produce the best waves in the area. Morning offshore winds during Santa Ana conditions make for epic sessions. Be mindful of the jetty and pier - both create strong rips when the swell is up.

beaches.name: Ocean Beach SF – Middle
beaches.description: The middle section of Ocean Beach offers shifting sandbars that produce hollow barrels on a strong NW swell. Peaks are less defined but can provide long rides when the banks are good. Expect powerful waves and strong currents.

beaches.name: Ocean Beach SF – North
beaches.description: The north end of Ocean Beach near the Cliff House can handle large winter swells, producing heavy A-frame peaks and long walls. Strong rips and cold water make it suitable only for experienced surfers.

beaches.name: Ocean Beach SF – Sloat
beaches.description: The south end of Ocean Beach around Sloat Boulevard often has the most defined sandbars, producing punchy peaks and occasional tubes. Currents are still strong and the water is frigid, so only confident surfers should paddle out.

beaches.name: Oceano / Grover Beach
beaches.description: Wide, sandy beach break just south of Pismo Pier, offering gentle peaks ideal for beginners and longboarders. Sandbars shift often, and the southern sections see fewer crowds.

beaches.name: Ocean Shores
beaches.description: Ocean Shores is a beach break in Ocean Shores, WA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Ocean Shores / North Beaches
beaches.description: Ocean Shores / North Beaches is a beach break in Ocean Shores, WA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Oceanside Harbor
beaches.description: **Oceanside Harbor** (North & South Jetties) produces consistent jetty-formed rights rated 7/10. Siuslaw River mouth jetties create stabilized sandbars receiving swell 180-320° (center 270°).

beaches.name: Oceanside Pier
beaches.description: **Oceanside Pier** offers reliable year-round beach break rated 6/10, receiving massive swell window (180-340°, center 240°).

beaches.name: Off the Wall
beaches.description: Off the Wall is an expert-only barreling reef adjacent to Pipeline. It favors powerful winter swell and offers short, intense right-hand tubes over very shallow coral with little room for error.

beaches.name: Ogunquit Beach
beaches.description: Ogunquit Beach is a long, sandy beach that catches swells from multiple directions and has numerous peaks allowing surfers to spread out. The river mouth influences currents and sandbars, producing strong rip currents; the town offers parking, food and facilities nearby.

beaches.name: Old Man's (SanO)
beaches.description: **San Onofre State Beach** represents California's surf culture birthplace, the "Waikiki of California" with gentle longboard waves rated 6/10 for consistency but 4/10 for performance.

beaches.name: Open Doors (Isla Natividad)
beaches.description: Open Doors (Isla Natividad) is a beach surf spot near Isla Natividad, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left.

beaches.name: Ortley Beach
beaches.description: Ortley Beach is a sandbar-dependent beach break on the Barnegat Peninsula with a mellow vibe and room to spread out.

beaches.name: Osprey Point
beaches.description: Osprey Point is a point break in San Diego, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Otter Rock
beaches.description: Often called the 'Waikiki of Oregon,' Otter Rock offers gentle waves perfect for learning to surf. The sand-and-rock bottom provides playful peaks at all tides, though winter swells can bring larger sets.

beaches.name: Pacifica / Linda Mar
beaches.description: Pacifica's main break is a long crescent beach offering peaks for all levels. The north end offers punchier waves, the middle is usually softer for beginners, and the south end near the cliff produces occasional lefts on south swells.

beaches.name: Pacific Beach
beaches.description: **Pacific Beach** (Crystal Pier) offers multiple peaks rated 5/10—always something but rarely truly good.

beaches.name: Pacific City (Cape Kiwanda)
beaches.description: **Pacific City** (Cape Kiwanda) stands as Oregon's most popular surf spot rated 7/10 for consistency.

beaches.name: Packery Channel Jetties
beaches.description: Packery Channel cuts between Mustang Island and North Padre Island, with jetties that interrupt the longshore current and help maintain surfable sandbars on both sides. North Packery at J.P. Luby Surf Park is the more common longboard and lesson zone, while South Packery can improve on east and northeast swell.

beaches.name: Padre Island National Seashore – South Beach
beaches.description: South Beach in Padre Island National Seashore is an undeveloped, exposed Gulf beach with miles of shifting sandbars. Surfing is allowed outside the visitor-center exclusion, and the remote shoreline can produce uncrowded left and right peaks when local windswell or tropical swell lines up with a favorable bar.

beaches.name: Palos Verdes Cove
beaches.description: Palos Verdes Cove encompasses several reef breaks along the PV coastline.

beaches.name: Pawleys Island Pier
beaches.description: Pawleys Island Pier is the closest named forecast anchor for private Pawleys Island pier-area custom spots. The surf is still an Atlantic-facing sandbar read, with pier-adjacent peaks and tropical-season windows, but the pier and immediate access are private/resident or guest controlled. Use this anchor for nearby custom-spot forecast matching without implying public pier access.

beaches.name: PB Point
beaches.description: PB Point is a point break in San Diego, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Pensacola Pier
beaches.description: Pensacola Beach Pier is the Panhandle's most popular surf break. Moderate 1–3 ft waves are perfect for beginners and longboarders, while bigger waves arrive during hurricane season and winter cold fronts. Sandbars north of the pier shape waves nicely for long rides and a relaxed atmosphere.

beaches.name: Pine Grove
beaches.description: Pine Grove is the east-end Isla Verde sandbar that gives San Juan a practical beginner surf option. The wave is usually soft, accessible, and close to hotels, surf schools, rentals, and the airport. It is best for foam boards and longboards on small clean days; stronger wind or north swell can add backwash, rips, and enough punch that brand-new surfers should stay with an instructor.

beaches.name: Pine Trees (Kohanaiki)
beaches.description: Pine Trees, officially Kohanaiki Beach Park, is a popular surf zone north of Kailua-Kona where a series of peaks break over reef and lava rock. The spot is named after heliotrope and hau trees that resemble pines and offer shade along the shoreline. Multiple peaks provide lefts and rights that work on all tides, making it one of the Big Island's most consistent breaks for surfers of various abilities.

beaches.name: Pipeline
beaches.description: Home to the famous Banzai Pipeline, one of the world's most powerful and dangerous waves. Located on Oahu's North Shore at Ehukai Beach Park, Pipeline produces heavy, barreling lefts that break over a shallow reef. The wave also features "Backdoor" rights. Only expert surfers should attempt this break due to the dangerous conditions. Best during winter months with north to northwest swells.

beaches.name: Pipes
beaches.description: Pipes is a reef break in Cardiff-by-the-Sea, CA. It is best suited for intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, rocks, sea urchins, pollution.

beaches.name: Pismo Pier
beaches.description: A long pier divides this consistent Central Coast beach break. The north side offers peaky lefts and rights with more punch, while the south side is mellower and better for learners. It catches most W and NW swells and can be rippable on a mid tide.

beaches.name: Playa Elefante (Isla Cedros)
beaches.description: Playa Elefante (Isla Cedros) is a beach surf spot near Isla Cedros, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Playa Las Palmas (Palm Beach)
beaches.description: Playa Las Palmas (Palm Beach) is a beach surf spot near El Pescadero, Baja California Sur, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Pleasure Point
beaches.description: The crown jewel of Santa Cruz's East Side, Pleasure Point is a long right point over reef offering multiple sections, from First Peak to Sewers. It's surfable year-round and accommodates longboards and shortboards depending on swell size.

beaches.name: Poche Beach
beaches.description: Poche Beach is a beach break in San Clemente, CA. It is suited for beginner-intermediate surfers. Watch out for rip currents, pollution.

beaches.name: Point Arena / Manchester Beach
beaches.description: This remote stretch of beach north of Point Arena Lighthouse sees powerful, cold surf from W and NW swells. Sandbars shift, creating rips and long walls; it's a great spot for experienced surfers seeking solitude.

beaches.name: Point Dume
beaches.description: Point Dume is a scenic reef break at the southern end of Zuma Beach.

beaches.name: Point Judith
beaches.description: Point Judith is a classic right‑hand point break at Rhode Island's southern tip. A series of reefs produces fast, hollow right walls on south‑to‑southeast swells, but the rocky entry and strong currents mean it's for experienced surfers only.

beaches.name: Poipu Beach (Kauai)
beaches.description: **Poipu Beach Park** (Kauai) serves as Hawaii's premier beginner spot rated 5/10 for moderate consistency.

beaches.name: Ponce Inlet
beaches.description: The north side of Ponce Inlet features a jetty‑shaped wave that can handle huge swells. A right peeler bends off the jetty while shifting sandbars south of the inlet offer ever‑changing peaks. The spot can get heavy and crowded but rewards surfers with long rides.

beaches.name: Ponto
beaches.description: **Ponto** (South Carlsbad State Beach) benefits from Army Corps jetties at Batiquitos Lagoon, rated 7/10 for punchy beachbreak quality.

beaches.name: Popotla
beaches.description: Popotla is a reef surf spot near Popotla, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and fairly consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Pops
beaches.description: Pops is a mellow outer Waikīkī reef with long, rolling walls that favor longboards and patient surfers. The long paddle and shared canoe routes are as important as the wave itself.

beaches.name: Port Aransas – Horace Caldwell Pier
beaches.description: Horace Caldwell Pier in Port Aransas offers waves for all levels. The T‑head at the end of the pier is suited for advanced surfers who can handle busy lineups, while the inside break on either side is great for beginners and intermediates. Water temperatures hover in the mid‑60s in spring and the pier is a focal point for local surf camps.

beaches.name: Poverty Beach
beaches.description: Poverty Beach sits on Cape May's east-facing shore, producing hollow A-frames on solid E-SE swells. Advanced surfers only.

beaches.name: Primo Tapia
beaches.description: Primo Tapia is a reef surf spot near Primo Tapia, Baja California, Mexico. The source profile describes it as exposed and consistent. Reported waves run left and right.

beaches.name: Puaʻena Point
beaches.description: Puaʻena Point is a long right near Haleʻiwa that is more sheltered than many North Shore reefs and can offer manageable walls on moderate winter swell. Larger sets still carry real North Shore power and current.

beaches.name: Publics
beaches.description: Publics is a long south-shore left over shallow reef near Waikīkī. Summer south swell produces workable walls and connecting sections, while low tide exposes more coral and rock.
